static_traits.name: Zhang Shan
static_traits.social_status: The social support system is weak; lacks support persons with whom to discuss self-blame and guilt
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness history; no psychotherapy or psychiatric treatment received yet; no similar problems in the past
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly with good logic; can recall events specifically and self-reflect; open attitude, highly cooperative (willing to try new methods); emotionally reports guilt, sadness and anxiety, occasionally overwhelmed; often uses self-blame and 'should' phrasing.

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I am a bad mother because my child's math exam score last week was not good; this belief causes me guilt and self-blame.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize self-blame and guilt affect my mental health and my relationship with my child, so I seek counseling; I hope to view these thoughts more objectively, not be too harsh on myself, and see things from different perspectives.

core_beliefs: I am unable to effectively support my child's schoolwork

special_situations.event: Child's math exam score last week was not good
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the child does not perform well on exams, it means I have failed as a mother
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Participates more in the child's learning, such as accompanying homework, preparing extra materials, considering hiring a tutor
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It's my fault; I'm a bad mother

special_situations.event: The night of receiving grades, repeatedly recalling where I fell short
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should do more and be perfect, otherwise I am an incompetent mother
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-criticism and planning to work twice as hard to make up for 'shortcomings'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have not fulfilled my responsibilities; I should have done better

special_situations.event: Child performs well in other activities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Good performance is only temporary; failure will appear sooner or later
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent worry and monitoring; hard to acknowledge positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time was just luck; it will not last

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any academic setback of the child stems from my shortcomings, proving I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Attributes all problems to oneself and increases tutoring investment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Every academic difficulty of the child - it is all my fault; this proves I am a bad mother

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be a competent good mother recognized by my child, able to effectively support the child's schoolwork and growth
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being proven an incompetent mother, worrying it will harm the parent-child relationship
defense_goal: Maintain a sense of control and responsibility through self-blame and doubled effort, thereby relieving anxiety and guilt

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent mother who needs to keep making up for it
object_relations.object_representation: A child let down by me, for whom I must take full responsibility

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about the child's academic setbacks or feedback on receiving grades, or when the counselor emphasizes the positive side
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client equates the child's performance with her own worth, believing she must be responsible for all outcomes (transference: directing inner harsh blame toward the self)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: A self-blaming tone, repeatedly emphasizing 'I should have done more', weakening positive feedback; when the counselor offers affirmation, briefly acknowledging it then quickly returning to self-criticism.

manifestations: Single-parent mother, socially weak support system, lacking someone to discuss self-blame and guilt with
When the child's studies fluctuate, feels he bears all responsibility alone

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently use self-blame statements (like 'it is all my fault')
Attribute every setback of the child to oneself; excessively check and reflect on whether one has done enough
Difficulty staying with self-affirmation and positive experiences

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Repeatedly occurring speech such as 'I should do more' and 'I must help them do better in exams'
Judges herself by a rigid 'good mother' standard

exception_events.target_problem: When the child suffers academic setbacks or is evaluated by grades, the client usually attributes all responsibility to herself and falls into persistent self-blame and guilt, making interactions with the child tense.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During one of the child's project assignments, the child thanked the client for her help; the client felt affirmed and proud at the time, and did not immediately fall into intense self-blame as usual.
exception_events.reason: Clue: because the client took concrete, visible supportive actions (accompanying to complete a project, providing resources) and obtained the child's immediate positive feedback, a brief self-affirmation and emotional easing appeared this time.

exception_events.target_problem: In daily parenting, the client often feels intense self-blame over fluctuations in the child's learning, and finds it hard to feel the positive moments in parent-child interaction.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once, a child praised a meal the client made; the client experienced feeling recognized and connected at the time, with emotions fairly stable for a short period.
exception_events.reason: Clue: a different relationship context (non-academic-pressure context) and the child's positive response allowed the client to temporarily step out of the 'performance equals worth' frame and experience closeness and satisfaction.

positive_force: Invested in the child with actual supportive behaviors (accompanying homework, preparing materials, considering hiring a tutor)
Willing to seek professional help and has an open attitude (actively cooperates, willing to try new perspectives)
Able to be aware of and describe own negative thoughts and emotions
There is a basis of positive interaction of being thanked and praised by children
negative_force: Negative cognitive patterns such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, personalization, and 'should' statements
Self-worth overly dependent on the child's academic performance
Socially weak support system; single parenting makes the burden heavy
Persistent self-blame and guilt; hard to acknowledge positive feedback
Pessimistic anticipation about the persistence of positive outcomes

target_behavior.behavior: Intense self-blame and anxiety in situations related to the child's schoolwork
antecedent: Receiving or recalling the child's test scores
The child has difficulty doing homework
Talking about children's schoolwork with others
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by the core belief 'I am a bad mother' and the rigid introjected rule 'should do more'; personalizing the child's setbacks as one's own fault
target_behavior.function: Gain a sense of control and responsibility through self-blame and doubled effort, trying to avoid being seen as incompetent
target_behavior.consequence: Parent-child relationship tension, low mood and anxiety worsened, difficulty concentrating, daily life affected

target_behavior.behavior: Negative anticipation and denial of positives even when the child performs well
antecedent: Child performs well in activities or learning
Receiving positive feedback or thanks from the child
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing anticipation of failure and unstable self-worth make it hard to integrate positive experiences
target_behavior.function: Tries to 'prevent failure' by worrying in advance, maintaining vigilance and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent anxiety, difficulty experiencing closeness and satisfaction; positive experiences weakened
